# Command reference

Every command of the running app, as `penumbra-cli ctl <command>` or a control-channel request sends it (see [Control](../control.md)). `{a, b?}` lists the params, `?` marks optional ones.


## general

| command | |
|---|---|
| `ping` | Check that the control channel answers |

## app

| command | |
|---|---|
| `app.about` | What the About window shows: version, commit, licence, the third-party notices (their file and each licence with its number of crates), trademarks; {notices?}. notices: true opens the notices in the browser (not in headless runs) |

## audio

| command | |
|---|---|
| `audio.config` | Audio settings for this run: {enabled?} |
| `audio.devices` | The audio inputs of this machine: name, default, rate, channels, format |
| `audio.file_info` | What an audio.file plays: {path} gives file, codec, rate, channels, duration (s), in_memory, ready, error, position (s), playing, gaps (silences while decoding caught up), seeks, restarts, bad_packets |
| `audio.measure_latency` | Plays quiet clicks (at most -20 dBFS) on an output and finds them on an input: {output?, input?, channels?, clicks?, level?, latency?, buffer?}; input `loopback:<output>` records what the output plays. Reports ms from push to arrival per channel, and an output estimate. Takes some seconds |
| `audio.mute` | Mutes every audio output at once, a panic button: {mute?} (default true; false unmutes). For this run only |
| `audio.outputs` | The audio outputs of this machine: name, default, rate, channels, format |
| `audio.play` | An audio.instrument plays one note at its next frame, as if channel `lane` of play had crossed threshold there; wired or not:{path, lane? (default 0)}. An audio.file starts over from its start (lane is ignored). While the show is paused nothing sounds and the press is dropped |
| `audio.seek` | An audio.file jumps to `seconds` into its file at the next frame and plays on from there, with short fades (a looping file stays in its pass): {path, seconds}. Not while its position is bound to a channel |
| `audio.status` | Audio input streams (device, rate, channels, open, error, frames, glitches, peak per channel in dBFS) and output buses (device, open, error, rate, latency_ms with fill_ms and device_ms, underruns, overruns, glitches, limiter reduction per node and of the sum, muted) |

## audio_file_out

| command | |
|---|---|
| `audio_file_out.start` | Start recording an out.audio_file node to a new WAV file (its params say what and how): turns its record param on (an edit); {path}; answers with the status once the file is created, or with a note while no sound came yet |
| `audio_file_out.status` | Sound recordings: node, recording, finishing, done, file, opened, format, rate, channels, seconds, samples, bytes, gap_samples, cut_samples, refused, dropped, sources (out.audio nodes heard with source all, else null), error; {path?} |
| `audio_file_out.stop` | Stop an out.audio_file's recording and finish the file: turns record off (an edit); {path}; answers with the status |

## beats

| command | |
|---|---|
| `beats.analyze` | Finds the beats and downbeats of a sound file with the Beat This! network, and its envelopes (level, bands, onsets) as chan.beat_analysis measures them, in the background, and keeps both in a cache: {path (an audio.file or chan.beat_grid) or file (relative to the project), wait? (default true: answers when done, at most 600 s), again? (default false: starts over)}. A 4 minute track takes seconds, a 2 hour mix about 3 minutes. Replies as beats.status |
| `beats.arrange` | Writes the arrangement of a music stage from the sections of the file a chan.beat_grid reads, as one undoable edit: {path (the chan.beat_grid), table (a table.text, created when missing), sequence (a chan.sequence, created when missing), slots ({slot: [element paths]}, e.g. {floor: ["/blocks", "/mountains"], sky: ["/galaxy"]}; an element may be {path, weight} instead, e.g. {path: "/glider", weight: 3}, to come on three times as often as one of weight 1 (default 1, at most 100), and with stages: ["/stage"] to show only while one of those stages shows (elsewhere it stays at presence 0 and its slot takes another element): the first element of each slot is on at the start, slots take turns in name order, the slots named sky and mid stay on through a break, the slot post holds effects that are on or off each by itself (off in an intro, outro or break, on from a drop), every other slot (floor, ceiling) follows the floor's rules), stage? (a path, or a list of stages side by side; each gets warmth, and camera where it has that param), switch? (a param that picks the stage, e.g. "/stages.index" of a tex.switch, or a list of them; it fades on a tex.cross, for two stages, and on a tex.switch with blend on), intensity? (a param that gets intensity, e.g. "/stage.dim", or a list), fade_min? (s, default 2: the shortest fade from one row into the next, also where the music cuts), stage_fade? (s, default 4: the shortest fade into a row whose stage changes), dwell? (sections, default 3: an element on that long gives way at the next boundary with change 0.3 or more, its slot's turn or not; a slot its stage hides counts on; 0 turns it off), opening? (default true: the file's first section brings its slots in one after another on bar starts, sky first, then mid, the floor and the rest, the ceiling last, a row per step of at least 2 bars), gaps? ({build?, break?}: the share of the floor in gaps, default 0.3 in a build and 0.6 in a break)}. The table has a row per section: start, end, role, change, the presence of each element (the column is named as the element), warmth, intensity, camera (the stage's camera preset: low in a main section, higher in a build, high and wide on a drop, level in a break, a variant per track), stage (changes only at a track start with change 0.8 or more, at most once in 8 minutes, to the next stage in the list and back again: 0, 1, 2, 1, 0), gaps (the share of the floor broken off: only in a build and a break) and flight (how the glider flies: 0 along the lane's turns, 1 straight, 2 along the turns with a roll on a downbeat, 3 straight with a lean on each downbeat; straight in a break, a roll on a drop, the lean in a build, 0, 1 and 3 by turns from track to track elsewhere). A strong boundary into a main section may leave the stage and one slot alone, drawn from the section's seed. Edit the table by hand to override a row. The sequence gets a step per row, its clock on the grid's seconds. Beside the table it creates or updates <table>_now, _plus, _next, _diff, _ramp, _mix, _half, _snap, _jump and _pick; _mix has a channel per column that moves through each fade, _pick jumps to the next row half way through it. Binds each element's presence, warmth, camera, gap (on a stage that has it), flight (on an element that has it) and switch to them, and intensity. Run it again after the file changes: it overwrites the table |
| `beats.cancel` | Stops a sound file's beat analysis and the measuring of its levels: {path or file}. Its chan.beat_grid nodes keep the beats and levels found so far; beats.analyze starts it again |
| `beats.cues` | Writes a cue list into a chan.sequence from the sections of the file a chan.beat_grid reads, as one undoable edit: {path (the chan.beat_grid), sequence (the chan.sequence), level? (section: a step per section, the default; track: a step per track), pieces? (what names a step's piece: label, the kind of sound, kind0, kind1...; letter, A, B... within a track; track, track0, track1...; default label, track for level track), transition? (zone: a cross-fade through each blend between sections, the default; cut)}. Sets steps, names (piece k is in<k> of a tex.sequence) and lead_in 0, clears file, and binds clock to the grid's seconds. The show then follows the music through seeks, loops and the grid's offset. A step after a blend begins where the blend ends. Needs the sections: beats.analyze waits for them. Run it again after the file changes |
| `beats.grid` | The beats found in a sound file: {path or file, from? to? (s)} gives beats (those chan.beat_grid uses: passages the network counted at twice or half the tempo around them are folded back to it), downbeats (the bar starts chan.beat_grid uses, voted over 64 beats), found_beats (the network's beats before folding) and marked_downbeats (those the network marks one by one; irregular on DJ mixes), s into the file, between from and to, and final_until and complete as beats.status. sections lists the sections that overlap from to to, once found: start and end (s), bars, label (the kind of sound, the same number anywhere in the file where it sounds alike), letter (repeats within a track share it), track, track_start, strength (0 to 1), seed and zone [start, end] (s, the blend from the section before), and with the music bus energy, bass, density (onsets per beat), kick (share of beats with a kick), jump (energy minus the section before's), role (intro, break, build, drop, outro or main) and change (0 to 1: how strongly the music changes where the section begins); null before. Does not start an analysis |
| `beats.status` | How the beat analyses stand: {path or file} for one, nothing for all held. Per file: running, progress (0 to 1), beats, downbeats, final_until (s; the grid before it is final, null for none yet), complete, bpm (median), error, cancelled, seconds, envelopes {running, progress, known_until (s), complete, bytes, error}, sections {ready, running, tracks, sections, kinds, error} and bus {ready} (travelled, energy and drop on chan.beat_grid). The sections and the bus are found once beats and envelopes are complete |

| `calib.project` | Pixels of world points through a calibrated camera (null behind it); {camera, points: [[x,y,z],...]} |

## camera

| command | |
|---|---|
| `camera.exposure` | Check the camera's exposure before a match, flat field or scan, in a few seconds: each projector alone shows white, the camera's frames are read where it lights the picture. Reports per projector the brightest pixels (peak, of 255; aim for about 200), the median, the black, the share that clips and in which channels, the change from frame to frame (flicker) and of the rows between frames (banding: a shutter shorter than the projector's frame), a verdict (ok, clipped, dark, unsteady), stops to change by and advice; `ok` is false while any projector clips. {camera (tex.video_in path), projectors? (paths, default every active out.projector), area? ([x, y, w, h] of the camera picture, 0..1), frames? (camera frames per projector, 4), settle? (s, 0.5), timeout? (s, 5), wait? (false: start and answer at once; job.status follows it and keeps the reply; true)} |

## chan

| command | |
|---|---|
| `chan.press` | Press a chan.button as a click on its node does: {path, down?}. Momentary: without `down` a tap (1 for one frame), `down: true` holds it until `down: false`; no history entry. Toggle: a press flips `value` (an edit), `down: false` does nothing |
| `chan.read` | Cook a chan or audio node and read its channels (values now, for sound also peak and rms of the block; {samples: true} for all); {path, output?, samples?} |

## comp

| command | |
|---|---|
| `comp.collapse` | Group side-by-side nodes into a new component, ports where wires cross; {paths, name?} |
| `comp.expand` | Dissolve a component, its nodes move up beside it; {path} |
| `comp.library` | Component files in the project's components/, the user's library and penumbra's own library |
| `comp.load` | Add a component from a file or a library (by name); one in a folder of its own copies that folder's files into the project's library/<name>/ first; {file, path?} |
| `comp.remove` | Take a component file out of the library (into its removed/ folder); {name, place?: project \| library} |
| `comp.save` | Write a component to a file (default: the library, <name>.comp.ron); {path, file?} |

## cook

| command | |
|---|---|
| `cook.meter` | Pass times of the last 8 s: last, smoothed (1 s lag), median, 1 % high, max, cook thread busy; {samples?: [seconds ago, ms] per pass} |
| `cook.play` | Run or stop the show clock; {playing?} (default true) |
| `cook.stats` | Cook pass timings since the last reset: passes, slowest pass, longest gap, late frames, stalls; {reset?} |
| `cook.status` | Show clock, last cook pass, watched nodes, thumbnail policy |
| `cook.step` | Cook frames at once while stepping, each one frame of show time after the last (while the clock plays); {frames?} (default 1, at most 3600); answers with the frame and the pass |
| `cook.stepping` | Move the show clock only by cook.step, not by the timer or a projector's vsync, so a render or recording gets every frame whatever the machine's speed; off goes on from where the steps left it; {on?} (default true); answers with the frame |
| `cook.thumbnails` | The editor's thumbnails, kept with the project (settings thumbnails and thumbnail_every; one undo step); {mode?: always \| when_free \| never, every?: cook passes between two thumbnail cooks of a node, 1 = every frame} |

| `dmx.status` | DMX outputs (target, writers, device, open, error, frames, rate asked and measured, timings in ms) and inputs (listen, readers, open, error, packets, universes with their sources) |

|---|---|

| command | |
|---|---|

| command | |
|---|---|
| `ndi.sources` | The NDI sources on the network, this process's out.ndi nodes included (name as `PC (Source)`, address), and the NDI runtime in use. The first call starts looking: `settling` is true while the list may still be filling |

## node

| command | |
|---|---|
| `node.batch` | Apply ops as one all-or-nothing batch; {ops: [{op, ...}], label?} |
| `node.bind` | Drive a param (or one component, /t.translate.0) with a channel or a table cell: a text param takes a cell as it is or a number by format ("{.1} m"), a choice its entry by name or place; {param, from, channel?, cell?: {row?, col?}, format?} |
| `node.connect` | Connect an output to an input; without input: the first of its kind, or the next free one of a run (a composite's layers); {from, output?, to, input?} |
| `node.copy` | Copy side-by-side nodes with everything inside them; returns the text; {paths} |
| `node.create` | Create a node; {path, kind, params?} |
| `node.cut` | Copy side-by-side nodes, then delete them (one undo step); {paths} |
| `node.delete` | Delete a node and everything inside it; {path} |
| `node.disconnect` | Clear an input; {to, input} |
| `node.info` | One node: params, connections, cook status; {path} |
| `node.kinds` | Node types with their params, inputs, outputs and tags. With a param: its help (what it does, type, default, range, unit, what each choice does). With search: the types whose name contains the text or a tag starts with it (TouchDesigner names, file extensions), as the add dialog finds them; {kind?, param?, search?} |
| `node.list` | Nodes under a path; {path?, recursive?} |
| `node.lock` | Lock (hold outputs) or unlock a node; {path, locked?} |
| `node.memory` | Video memory per node, largest first. Also what the editor holds (pictures of geometry, display copies) and the render attachments that renderers of one size share. All of it against what wgpu has allocated, and wgpu's allocations by label; {limit?} (default 30 of each) |
| `node.paste` | Paste the nodes copied last (or `text`) into a component or the root; {into?, text?} |
| `node.place` | Move nodes in the editor; top left corner, graph units on their component's plane, one undo step. null leaves a node to the editor to place; {nodes: {path: [x, y]}} |
| `node.rename` | Rename a node; the expose lines and node references that name it follow, in the same undo step; {path, name} |
| `node.replace` | Replace a node with one of another kind under the same name (one undo step). Keeps the params, wires and bindings that fit and lists what was not kept; {path, kind} |
| `node.reset` | Start stateful nodes over (feedback, cache, time machine, tracker, filter...). A component resets the stateful nodes inside; locked nodes keep their outputs; {paths} or {path} |
| `node.set` | Set params, null resets to the default; {path, params: {name: value}} |
| `node.snapshot` | Cook a tex node (or a geo node: its picture) and write its output as PNG (8-bit sRGB); {path, output?, file? (relative to the project; default in the temp directory)} |
| `node.unbind` | Back to the param's stored value; {param} |
| `node.watch` | Cook a node every frame (or stop); {path, watch?} |

## project

| command | |
|---|---|
| `project.demo` | Open the demo project, made afresh: changes, state and layout from before are gone |
| `project.example` | Open a shipped example from a fresh copy in the user's data folder (the shipped one stays as it is). Changes last until the example is opened again; project.save_as keeps them; {name} |
| `project.examples` | The examples shipped with penumbra, by name, and where they lie |
| `project.info` | Project directory, unsaved changes, file errors, nodes that did not load (broken), who is editing |
| `project.new` | Make an empty project in dir (created if missing, must hold no project.ron) and open it; {dir} |
| `project.open` | Close this project (state saved, changes written) and open the one in dir; {dir} |
| `project.recent` | Recently opened projects, newest first (the demo is not listed), and the open one |
| `project.save` | Write project.ron now, also over a file that failed to merge (copied to project.ron.bak first) |
| `project.save_as` | Copy the open project (its files and the latest state snapshot) into dir (new or empty) and open the copy, a project of its own; {dir} |
| `project.settings` | Project settings with their values and what they do; {set?: {name: value}}, null resets (one undo step) |

## projector

| command | |
|---|---|
| `projector.flatfield` | Measure with a camera how brightness and colour vary across each projector's picture (hot spot, a colour cast towards an edge), and the brighter black where projectors overlap. Writes per projector a gain map and a black lift (gain_NAME.png, black_NAME.png) and connects them to out.projector's gain and black inputs. Blocks for about 20 s per projector; {camera (tex.video_in path), projectors (out.projector paths), scans (one scan folder per projector, with cam_to_proj.exr and proj_to_cam.exr, relative to the project; they must fit the current setup), even? (all: brightness and colour, measured on a flat evenly coloured surface \| colour: the colour cast only, which a relief's shading does not change), levels? (drive levels per primary, 5), low? (lowest level, sRGB-encoded drive, 0.6), frames? (camera frames averaged per picture, 4), settle? (s, 0.5), timeout? (s, 5), degree? (of the smooth surface fitted over the projector, 3), trim? (share of samples the fit may ignore, the surface's own pattern, 0.25), floor? (share of the picture allowed to stay dimmer than the target, 0.02), cover? (share of a projector's brightest that counts as lit for the black, 0.1), blur? (of the black lift, projector px, 6), contrast? (projector contrast, black = white / contrast, where the camera cannot read the black), out? (folder in the project, flatfield), apply? (true: connect the maps, one undo step), pictures? (false: also keep the camera's pictures, 16-bit sRGB PNGs, in out/pictures), check_exposure? (stop after the whites when the camera clips one, true), wait? (false: start and answer at once; job.status follows it; true)} |
| `projector.match` | Measure the projectors with a camera (each alone: black, white, red, green and blue ramps) and write their colour correction (matrix, curves) so they look alike. Blocks for about half a minute per projector; {camera (tex.video_in path), projectors? (paths, default every active out.projector), levels? (8), settle? (s, 0.5), samples? (curve samples, 17), area? ([x, y, w, h] of the camera picture, 0..1), timeout? (s, 5), target? (reference: the others respond like the reference projector, the reference keeps straight curves, works through any camera \| srgb: every projector follows the sRGB curve, only with a camera known to be linear), refine? (rounds of closed-loop correction against the reference, the matrix on white, then the curves on greys; 5; 0 off), grey_levels? (greys the curves are refined on, evenly spaced; 3), save? (folder, relative to the project: also measures a grey ramp and writes each projector's measurement as NAME.json with NAME the node name, to match from later), note? (text saved with them: settings, lamp hours), apply? (true: write the params as one undo step), check_exposure? (stop after the first pictures when the camera clips a projector's white, true), wait? (false: start and answer at once; job.status follows it and keeps the reply; true)}. Without the camera: {from (folder of NAME.json, or {projector path: file}), projectors?, samples?, apply?, wait?} matches from stored measurements; each camera channel follows the projector dimmest there, so the common white lies between the white points when no projector is the dimmest in every channel |
| `projector.test` | Switch the test pattern of every out.projector at once (its `test` and `test_pattern` params, one undo step): {on (true: the pattern instead of the input, false: the input again), pattern? (align: cells, centre cross, circle and edge, for keystone and alignment \| focus: one-pixel checkers and lines at the corners and the centre \| motion: bars and a frame strip moving on each presented frame, with the frame and late counts, for stutter and dropped frames after the GPU \| fields: full white, red, green, blue, black, projectors in turn, for dead pixels; unchanged when left out), projectors? (paths, default all)}. One projector showing a pattern draws it white; several draw in colours that keep overlapping ones apart |

## render

| `render.frame` | Move the view.camera wired into a tex.render so its geometry fills the picture; the direction stays (orthographic: sets its size); {path} |

## res

| command | |
|---|---|
| `res.analyze` | What the projectors need of every node they show: size, needed, verdict, suggestion. Waits up to 3 s for render nodes to measure (pending: those that did not) |
| `res.optimize` | Give the nodes the suggested sizes, one undoable entry; {paths?, dry_run?} (paths: only these) |
| `res.overlay` | Colour the mappers' and render nodes' pictures by resolution (green 1:1, red coarse, blue wasted); {on?} |

## scan

| command | |
|---|---|
| `scan.align` | Line projectors in a row or a column up from their scans (folders scan.capture or scan.decode wrote). Fits a homography camera -> projector per scan; the content is the camera-axis rectangle spanning all their frames. Writes per projector its mapper's region (its share of the content) and corners (where that share lands in the projector), fit stretch, as one undo step; {scans: [folder, ...], mappers? ([tex.mapper path, ...], one per scan; without them only the report), apply? (true; false: report only)} |
| `scan.blend` | Blend weights for projectors lighting the same surface, from their scans (folders scan.decode wrote). Writes weight_N.png (16-bit, sRGB-encoded so tex.image_file gives the weight; multiply the projector's picture by it), detail_N.png (1 where this projector is the sharpest of those lighting a spot, for tex.blend_weight's detail mode) and proj_to_cam_smooth_N.exr (the map smoothed, for tex.remap); {scans: [folder, ...], masks? ([file or null, ...], e.g. scan.objects' labels_N.png), out? (folder, objects), ramp? (projector px, 200), blur? (projector px, 3), reach? (camera px, 6), sigma? (projector px, 6), into_scans? (write weight.png, detail.png and proj_to_cam_smooth.exr into each scan's folder, where tex.scan reads them, false), wait? (false: start and answer at once, job.status follows it; true)} |
| `scan.cancel` | Stop the scan going on (scan.run) before its next picture. The projectors show their pictures again; the files of earlier scans stay; {} |
| `scan.capture` | Scan projectors with a camera, live. Each projector alone shows the structured light patterns (in its own pixels, past its colour correction, the network untouched) while the others show black. The camera's frames are decoded and written as scan.decode writes them, into out/<projector> (the path without its leading slash, slashes as _). Measures the light-to-camera latency on the way. Blocks about 15 s per projector; {camera (tex.video_in path), projectors? (paths, default every active out.projector), out? (folder, scan), settle? (s after the latency, 0.05), timeout? (s, 5), level? (signal of the lit stripes, 1), levels? (instead of level: a scan per level, e.g. [1, 0.4], merged per camera pixel, the surest decode winning, so the dim pass decodes where the bright one clips; the first level's colour; 1 to 4 levels), frames? (keep the camera frames as PNG in out/<projector>/frames, frames_1, ... per level, each with coding.json, the record scan.decode reads; false), verify? (take a picture only when two frames agree, true), retries? (frames that may disagree, 3), fill? (projector px, 32), options?: {min_contrast?, saturation?, min_confidence?, tolerance?, window? (camera px round a pixel over which the bits it resolves are judged, 7; 0 the whole picture), epipolar? (px a decoded pixel may lie off the geometry the decode as a whole obeys, else it is dropped: light thrown on by the walls decodes wrong, 4; 0 off)}, coding? (gray: Gray code alone, 46 pictures at 1080p, good to about a projector pixel; gray_phase: the Gray code down to stripes of half a period, then sines per axis, 54 pictures, good to a tenth of a pixel where the camera sees the sines; gray_phase), period? (gray_phase: the sines' period, 8, 16, 32 or 64 projector px; 16), steps? (gray_phase: sines per axis, 3 to 16; 8), gamma? (gray_phase: the projector's response, light = signal ^ gamma, so the sines leave it as sines; measure it or leave 2.2; 1 to 3)} |
| `scan.decode` | Decode a structured light scan from the camera's pictures of tex.scan_pattern 0, 1, 2, ... (files in a folder, sorted by name, numbers by value). Writes cam_to_proj.exr and proj_to_cam.exr (maps for tex.remap), scene.png (the scene as the projector sees it) and quality.png, and coding.json (how the scan was coded); {frames (folder, relative to the project; or a list of folders: scans of one projector at different levels of light, merged per camera pixel, the surest decode winning, the first's colour), projector?: [w, h] (the recorded size, else 1920, 1080), coding?, period?, steps? (as scan.capture took them; by default what coding.json in the frames folder or the one above records, else plain Gray or the default gray_phase by the number of pictures), out? (folder, default frames/decoded), fill? (projector px, 32), options?: {min_contrast?, saturation?, min_confidence?, tolerance?, window? (camera px round a pixel over which the bits it resolves are judged, 7; 0 the whole picture), epipolar? (px a decoded pixel may lie off the geometry the decode as a whole obeys, else it is dropped: light thrown on by the walls decodes wrong, 4; 0 off)}} |
| `scan.face_template` | Writes per face of a scene a folder (scene/faces/<face>) with a template for content delivered for that face and the maps tex.face_content puts it on the face with. A face that is a quadrilateral is rectified (u and v along its edges): its corners given to scan.scene, the straight corners scan.regions found, or four edges fitted to its border; its aspect given, else estimated from the perspective of the corners. Any other face is framed by its bounding box in the camera's picture. Files: template.png (the face rectified at the template's size: the camera's photo of it, outside dimmed, the face's edge and a grid in true squares), mask.png (white the face, grey an object in front of it, black not the face), uv.png (camera size, 16-bit: red u, green v, blue 1 on the face, for previewing a delivery on the camera's photo), uv_camera.exr and uv_N.exr per projector (as scan.scene's uv files), face.json (name, size, aspect, corners); faces.json lists all written. {scene? (folder, scene), faces? ([name or number, or {face, aspect? [width, height], corners? [[x, y] x 4] camera px, far left first, clockwise}, ...]; all regions when the scene has any, else all faces, leaving out those under min_pixels), size? (template's longer side, px, 1920), photo? (the camera's picture of the scene; the first scan's photo.png or frames/00.png), min_pixels? (camera px, a thousandth of the picture), focal? (the camera's focal length in pixels of its picture, for the aspects and normals; else told by the faces' corners where the camera sees them in perspective, or assumed 1.5 times the picture's width)} |
| `scan.faces` | The faces of a scene, by the names tex.face_content and scan.face_template take: every region of scan.regions (by its name, else `region N`) and every face of scan.scene (`face N`), with its size in camera pixels, whether its template exists and its normal in the camera's frame where known (a rectified face). {scene? (folder scan.scene wrote, scene)} |
| `scan.folders` | The scans in the project, what scan.blend and projector.flatfield take as scans: every folder (up to 4 deep, not state or library) holding cam_to_proj.exr and proj_to_cam.exr, with the out.projector it belongs to (the one a tex.scan writing it names, else the one it is named after), the tex.scan, whether scan.blend wrote its weight into it, and when its map was written (unix seconds); {} |
| `scan.objects` | Find the objects in front of a surface by parallax, per projector, between a scan of the empty scene (reference) and a scan with the objects (folders scan.decode wrote). The objects are numbered alike in every projector, top of the camera picture first. Writes per projector labels_N.png (8-bit, 0 background, k the object) and parts_N.png, plus objects_camera.png (the same labels in camera space, for shapes.trace with labels) and objects_camera_view.png; {projectors: [{reference, scan}, ...], out? (folder, objects), threshold? (camera px, 25), split? (camera px per projector px, 2), min_area? (projector px, 1/256 of the projector), erode? (projector px, 2), unmeasured? (projector px, 4), rim? (projector px, 25)} |
| `scan.patterns` | The pictures of a structured light scan in the order scan.capture shows them (tex.scan_pattern shows plain Gray code only); {projector?: [w, h] (1920, 1080), coding?, period?, steps? (as scan.capture)} |
| `scan.regions` | The faces scan.scene found grouped into regions, one per part of the scene content treats as one (a crate's front with its rib strips and rims, a lid, a side), cleaned up (seams between a region's faces closed, holes filled, the ragged edge smoothed, four straight edges where the region is a quadrilateral, else straight borders where a line fits, as in scan.scene) and the floor switched off. The grouping is a list of regions, each a set of seed pixels in the camera picture (the face under each seed, or the nearest one within reach, belongs to it), an optional name and an optional enabled flag; faces under no seed are regions of their own; a region is enabled unless it says otherwise or lies mostly on the floor (found from the faces' planes against the support). It is kept in a file (regions.json in the scene folder) that `regions` replaces and `edit` changes: [{op: merge, at: [[x, y], ...], name?} (the faces under the points, and the regions they are in, become one region), {op: split, at: [x, y]} (the face under it leaves its region), {op: disable \| enable \| auto, at} (its region off, on, or back to the default), {op: name, at, name}, {op: clear}]. Writes regions_camera.png and regions_N.png per projector (8-bit, 0 none or disabled, enabled regions numbered top of the camera picture first; drop-in replacements for planes_camera.png and planes_N.png), regions_view.png (regions in colour, disabled faces striped grey, seeds as dots) and regions_reply.json (the reply: per region its faces, seeds, kind floor/level/upright, size, straight corners and per projector its plane; the faces with a pixel inside each to address them by; suggestions: thin faces lying on the plane of a large one they touch, rib strips next to their panel). {scene? (folder scan.scene wrote, scene), file? (the grouping, scene/regions.json), regions? ([{name?, seeds: [[x, y], ...], enabled?}, ...], replaces the file's), edit? ([op, ...], applied to the file's), out? (folder, the scene folder), seam? (camera px, 10), smooth? (camera px, 2.5), straight? (true), reach? (camera px, 12)} |
| `scan.relief` | Height maps of a mostly flat object (a relief panel) from its scans (folders scan.capture or scan.decode wrote), no reference scan needed. Per projector: a robust plane projector -> camera, the residual along its main direction as the height, the panel cut out at jumps, holes filled. Every projector is brought to the first one's units over the camera pixels both light (symmetric fit). Writes height_N.exr (0 to 1 over the heights' 1st to 99.5th percentile, for tex.lookup), mask_N.png (the light mask, for tex.image_file or scan.blend's masks), height_camera.exr and relief_view.png (the same in camera space, to look at); {scans: [folder, ...], out? (folder, relief), sign? ("auto" \| 1 \| -1: the first projector's sign, the others follow it by the overlap; auto is a heuristic, the wall around the panel taken as behind it; 1 and -1 are fixed to the camera's axes; the reply's sign.as_param pins what a run found), scale? ("symmetric" \| "least_squares"), jump? (camera px per projector px, 4), erode? (projector px, 4), reach? (projector px, 60: notches in the measured panel's outline up to twice this wide are lit, nothing past it)} |
| `scan.run` | The scan button of tex.scan nodes. Scans their projectors one after another with their camera (scan.capture, each into the node's folder), lines them up if every node names its mapper (scan.align, one undo step) and writes blend weights and smoothed maps into the scan folders (scan.blend); the nodes then show them. Runs in the background (scan.status, scan.cancel); {nodes? (tex.scan paths, default every tex.scan; all must name the same camera), wait? (return when done, with the report, false)} |
| `scan.scene` | Flat faces and the objects among them from one scan per projector (folders scan.capture or scan.decode wrote), no reference scan needed: every flat face (floor, wall, each face of each box) fits a homography of its own; they are found one fit after the other by RANSAC until no fit holds a face of min_plane, coplanar faces that do not touch (the tops of two boxes side by side) split into faces of their own, patches of curved surfaces dropped. What fits no face is an object; the face right below the objects is the support. Any face that is a rectangle of known aspect can be rectified: its four edges in the camera picture, completed where hidden, give the homography to its u and v. Borders between faces are straight where the measured one is a line (two faces meeting at a crease on the line their planes cross in, where every projector agrees and the measured border lies on it; else a fitted line with corners); where no line fits (curved or ragged borders) and along objects they stay as measured. Writes per projector planes_N.png and labels_N.png (8-bit, 0 none, k the face or object, numbered alike in every projector; labels_N.png as scan.objects writes it), scene_N.png (faces in colour, objects white), uv_K_N.exr per rectified face K (red and green its u along the outline's first edge and v along its last, 0 to 1; blue 1 on the face, also where nothing was measured, 0.5 on an object, 0.25 on another face; -1 outside the outline), height_N.exr and mask_N.png (the objects' height over the support, as scan.relief writes them); in camera space planes_camera.png, objects_camera.png, uv_K_camera.exr, height_camera.exr and scene_view.png (with the rectified faces' outlines and a grid in true squares); scene.json (the reply: per face its plane fit in each projector, projector_to_camera and camera_to_projector; per rectified face its homographies between camera, projectors and uv and its normal in the camera's frame; `coordinates` names the frames). {scans: [folder, ...], out? (folder, scene), rectify? ([{plane?, aspect: [width, depth], corners? ([[x, y] x 4] camera px, instead of finding them; without plane they give the face: the plane most pixels inside lie on, taken from the faces and objects it was split into, also where it sags a little)}, ...], else the support at 60:40), support? (plane number, or "rectified" for the first face in rectify; else the one below the objects), sign?, scale? (as scan.relief), tolerance? (camera px a pixel may lie off its face, 2), min_plane? (share of the measured pixels, 0.002), max_planes? (most faces kept, 255), min_object? (projector px, 1/256 of the projector), erode? (projector px the light mask shrinks, 2), straight? (straight borders in planes_camera.png and planes_N.png, true; planes_camera_measured.png keeps the measured ones), straight_tolerance? (camera px nine tenths of a measured border may lie off its line, 2), straight_length? (shortest straight border, px, 16), focal? (the camera's focal length in pixels of its picture, for the normals; else told by the rectified faces' corners, or assumed 1.5 times the picture's width)} |
| `scan.status` | How the scans of the tex.scan nodes stand: running, progress (0 to 1), step, the last run's error and warnings; {} |
| `scan.synthetic` | Writes the scans of a made-up room, ray cast, as scan.decode writes real ones: for trying scan.scene and the content after it without projectors or a camera. The room "pumpkin" is a landscape of five Euro crates with a ribbed pumpkin on one of them, two projectors left and right of the camera, decode noise like a real scan's; "landscape" three crates and a ball, "crate" one crate and a ball (both small and nearly noise free, as the tests use them). Writes per projector a folder (a, b) with proj_to_cam.exr, cam_to_proj.exr, scene.png and quality.png, and photo.png (the camera's picture of the room lit white by that projector, which a real decode does not write). {room? (pumpkin, landscape or crate; pumpkin), out? (folder, synthetic), scale? (pumpkin: camera and projectors are scale times 480 x 270 pixels, 0.25 to 8; 4, full HD), noise? (camera px, the standard deviation of the decode noise per axis; pumpkin 0.15 times scale), outliers? (share of pixels decoded far off, 0 to 0.1; pumpkin 0.002)} |
